grand_strategy.reading:
Croatia plays the strategy of a small state that has solved its existential
question - NATO and the EU - and is now spending the dividend. Its first
objective is no longer to be admitted but to make Serbia's rearmament and
its own memory politics the neighbour's problem: it deters from inside the
Alliance, speaks to Belgrade in the voice of a member state (conditionality
on the missing, a reported weapons purchase, a defence declaration with
Tirana and Pristina) and keeps the instruments that are not its own - the
US licence on JANAF, EU loans for tanks, the High Representative in
Sarajevo - within reach. The Luttwakian pattern is that every lever is
borrowed and every success invites the response it was meant to prevent:
deterrence feeds Serbian rearmament, a refusal to receive Vucic hands him
the memorial stage, discipline on Russian oil prices out a Hungarian
partner it needs for INA. Domestically the strategy has two authors:
Plenkovic, EU-centred, tied to a Homeland Movement coalition, and
Milanovic, re-elected with 74.9%, who vetoes deployments and cancels
summits; Belgrade reads the harder voice. Two signals that are not
rows: Orban's fall in April 2026 has changed the weather with Hungary
overnight, and Serbia's snap election of 25 October 2026 may reset a tone
that Zagreb has so far refused to reset. Bosnia, where Zagreb's kin are
a constituent people dependent on imposed rules, is the arena in which
its soft power is thinnest.

stances_toward.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). 'Rival', not 'adversary': Croatia wants the issues settled, not Montenegro defeated. Bond - grievance: the 1991-92 Morinj camp, the Prevlaka and Jadran disputes, and the 2024 Jasenovac resolution.
